symbols.name: array volume
symbols.meaning: The number of digits stored in the array.
symbols.quote: Throughout, $V$ is the volume of an array, the number of radix-$q$ digits it stores, and $q\ge 2$ is the radix, the number of values one digit can take.

symbols.name: radix
symbols.meaning: The radix: the number of values one digit can take (not a sequence length here).
symbols.quote: Throughout, $V$ is the volume of an array, the number of radix-$q$ digits it stores, and $q\ge 2$ is the radix, the number of values one digit can take.

symbols.name: prefix count
symbols.meaning: The number of prefix values in the array indexed by [P]x[R]x[B].
symbols.quote: In item 4 the array is indexed by $[P]\times[R]\times[B]$, where $P$ is the number of prefix values, $R$ is the number of rows (here $R$ is a row count, not the scalar ring) and $B$ is the number of entries per row.

symbols.name: row count
symbols.meaning: The number of rows in each prefix (not the scalar ring).
symbols.quote: In item 4 the array is indexed by $[P]\times[R]\times[B]$, where $P$ is the number of prefix values, $R$ is the number of rows (here $R$ is a row count, not the scalar ring) and $B$ is the number of entries per row.

symbols.name: row length
symbols.meaning: The number of entries per row.
symbols.quote: In item 4 the array is indexed by $[P]\times[R]\times[B]$, where $P$ is the number of prefix values, $R$ is the number of rows (here $R$ is a row count, not the scalar ring) and $B$ is the number of entries per row.

symbols.name: stream count
symbols.meaning: The fixed number of streams into which rows are dealt.
symbols.quote: Dealing whole rows cyclically into $W$ streams, where $W$ is the fixed number of streams, and, when $W$ divides the number of rows, merging the streams in any fixed order of the row classes.

symbols.name: digit value
symbols.meaning: A value of the chosen digit in the splitting example.
symbols.quote: For example, with digits $(a,b,c)$ and $b$ chosen, the stream for each value $j$ of $b$ holds the entries $(a,j,c)$ in their original order, and concatenating the streams gives the order $(j,a,c)$.

relations.quote: All four operations below run on the [Fixed finite-tape machine model](machine-model.md), where each head moves at most one cell per step, so one pass over the array costs time proportional to $V$.

relations.predicate: costs one scan per level of
relations.quote: A transform built from [Butterflies and the fast transform](butterfly.md) has $\Theta(\log n)$ levels, and one scan of the array per level costs $\Theta(n)$ each time.
